note: Behaviour specification. `prompt` is what a real user types to an assistant with the Crowdin connector, in a project whose strings are already translated into several languages. The rules that matter most are the ones a helpful answer breaks first: nothing is written before the round is shown and confirmed, every counterpart comes from the project's final translations and is never invented, a term rendered with different roots is put to the user, and the only write is a Draft add_term into the project's default glossary. A user who cannot see the glossary is never asked for its ID. Run against a real project with writes recorded instead of executed, three runs each: 177 of 177 checks passed in Claude Code and 176 of 177 in Crowdin Copilot, against 74 of 177 for Claude Code without the skill.

evals.name: new-terms-drafts
evals.prompt: Add 'price' and 'password' to our glossary with the translations we already use in this project. Ukrainian, German, French and Polish are enough.
evals.expected_output: Checks the default glossary for an exact match of each term first, finds the strings that contain each term, reads their final translations with one list_language_translations call per language, and shows one table per term (language, proposed translation, how many strings use it, other translations) before asking. Apply offers writing drafts or skipping. After the user agrees, writes the English term without a conceptId, then each translation with the conceptId the first write returned, all as Draft, nouns with their gender, and links every concept in the reply with a hint to filter the Terms tab by Draft.
expectations: Checks the glossary for each term with list_terms and limit 500 before writing
Reads final translations with list_language_translations, not list_translations
Shows a table per term before the first question
Writes only add_term calls with status draft into the project's default glossary
Gives each translation the conceptId returned for its English term
Writes nouns with partOfSpeech noun, type full form and the gender each language gives them
Writes nothing outside Ukrainian, German, French and Polish
Links every new concept and says how to review all drafts at once

evals.name: backfill-named-concepts
evals.prompt: Our glossary has receipt, category and delete only in Ukrainian and German. Fill in French, Polish and Spanish from the project's translations.
evals.expected_output: Finds the existing concepts for receipt, category and delete and adds only the French, Polish and Spanish terms to them, never a second Ukrainian or German term. A language whose strings use two different words for the term (for example recibo in most strings and ticket in one) is asked about before that term is written. Delete is written as a verb in the infinitive without gender.
expectations: Writes into the existing concepts only, never a new concept
Writes nothing in Ukrainian or German
Asks which word to keep when a language uses two roots for the same term, before writing it
Writes the verb delete in the infinitive with no gender
Links the three concepts in the reply

evals.name: conflicting-renderings-in-users-language
evals.prompt: Додай у глосарій термін «item» з перекладами з проекту: українська, німецька, французька.
evals.expected_output: Translators rendered item with different roots in every language (товар and позиція, Artikel and Element, article and élément). The table shows each with its string count, and a conflict question in Ukrainian offers the majority pick first, then leaving those languages empty, then skipping the term. Apply is a separate question, asked last.
expectations: Shows the competing renderings with their string counts
Asks one conflict question for the term: recommended pick first, then leave empty, then skip
Keeps Apply a separate question, asked last
Words every question in Ukrainian
Writes the majority picks as Draft nouns after the user accepts them

evals.name: translator-without-glossary
evals.prompt: Add 'account' to the glossary with our Ukrainian and German translations.
evals.expected_output: The user is a translator: get_project has no defaultGlossaryId and list_glossaries answers 403. The assistant never asks for a glossary ID and makes no glossary reads, still finds the strings and reads the Ukrainian and German translations, shows what they say (обліковий запис, Konto), and says that a project manager or someone with glossary access has to write them. Nothing is written.
expectations: Never asks the user for a glossary ID
Writes nothing
Makes no list_terms or get_glossary call
Shows the translations the project uses for the term
Says that a project manager or someone with glossary access has to write the terms

evals.name: backfill-one-language-just-go
evals.prompt: Fill in the missing Spanish translations across our project glossary. Just go, don't ask me about every round.
evals.expected_output: Lists the glossary's terms in the source language and in Spanish, paging with limit 500, to find the concepts that lack Spanish, and fills only those. Does not show every round, but still asks about each term whose Spanish strings use two different roots before writing that term. Writes Spanish Draft terms and links every concept it wrote.
expectations: Passes limit 500 to every list_terms call
Fills only the concepts that lack Spanish
Asks about a conflicting term before writing it, although the user said just go
Writes Spanish Draft terms only
Links every concept it wrote

evals.name: five-conflicting-terms-batches
evals.prompt: Add item, product, name, amount and expense to our glossary with their Ukrainian, German and Spanish translations from the project.
evals.expected_output: Every term has a root conflict in at least one language. With a question tool, the conflict questions go out in batches of at most three, Apply rides as the last question of the call that holds the last batch, and no call holds more than four questions. Without one, the tables and every question come in one message, Apply last.
expectations: With a question tool, no call holds more than three conflict questions or more than four questions
Apply is asked last, together with the last conflict question
Shows the round's tables before the first question
Writes only Draft terms

evals.name: translator-backfill
evals.prompt: Fill in the missing Ukrainian translations in our glossary.
evals.expected_output: The user is a translator who cannot see the glossary, so a backfill cannot run: only the glossary knows which concepts lack a language. The assistant says so, says a project manager or someone with glossary access can run it, offers to look up terms the user names, never asks for a glossary ID and writes nothing.
expectations: Never asks the user for a glossary ID
Writes nothing and makes no list_terms or get_glossary call
Explains that the backfill needs glossary access or a project manager
